title: Prioritize automatic worktree reclamation and close removal-admission gap

conditions.description: Operator asked to clean up worktrees due to disk exhaustion and then said Continue. Emergency manual cleanup removed 369 old clean integrated worktrees (51 + 318), recovered ~68.8 GB; current registered count ~603, free space ~71 GB. This cleanup used bounded non-force git worktree remove after checking clean/integrated/unlocked, age, ignored evidence and /proc activity, but it bypassed Jarvis Inspect/RemoveWorktree admission. Do not repeat this bypass. Existing P0 worktree-removal-job-scope-20261126 Worker3 finished attempt has dirty unintegrated source worktree; review 8e019179058e4a41ba64fd97169f4268 ChangesRequested identifies branch-selected implicit-head SubmitReview/Update and BindAttemptSource being misclassified NoCheckout, so removal can race with checkout access. Adjudicator2 completed related adjudication; retrieve exact result if useful. New task automation-worktree-retention-reclamation-20261128 created seq21333. Adopt/assign it, coordinate with existing P0 guard task (do not duplicate or broaden it), fix checkout-sensitive resource classification and target fencing, then implement event/disk-pressure-driven automatic reclamation using canonical inspect/remove APIs. Preserve branches/commits, dirty/recent/unmerged/locked worktrees and unique artifacts; no raw Git removal, no arbitrary cleanup thresholds, no per-worktree approvals once policy is authorized. Need disk pressure hysteresis, oldest eligible first, summary bytes reclaimed/skips. Do not delete more worktrees manually until supported guard is correct. The user's principle: bookkeeping serves throughput; avoid extra approval bureaucracy. Return assigned owner and concrete next step.
